variants.name: Razor views / Razor Pages (.cshtml)
variants.implementation_notes: Razor is the dominant C# realization: .cshtml files mix literal HTML with @ expressions, @model types the view model, _Layout/_ViewStart supply the shared chrome and partial views or tag helpers compose fragments, and the Razor SDK compiles each view to a C# class - so a marker that does not exist on the model is a build error rather than an empty region. Razor Pages (Pages/*.cshtml with a PageModel) is the same mechanism with the page owning its handler instead of a controller action.
variants.idiom_name: Razor .cshtml views with @model, layouts and partial views
pitfalls: Razor encodes @expressions by default, but Html.Raw (and IHtmlContent built by hand) bypasses it: every raw mark is a security review item.
The _ViewImports/_ViewStart chain is implicit; a view can inherit a model type, layout and tag helpers from files it never mentions, which makes behaviour hard to trace.
Templates are compiled: without runtime compilation enabled, an edited .cshtml needs a rebuild before the change appears, and the view cache must be cleared in production.

variants.name: Scriban runtime text templating (Liquid-compatible)
variants.implementation_notes: Scriban is the engine for output that is not an MVC view: parse a template string or file with Template.Parse (Template.ParseLiquid for Liquid syntax), render against a POCO or dictionary model, and let the default member renaming expose PascalCase properties as snake_case names. It is the usual choice for HTML email bodies, generated code or text files, and for background workers and console tools where the Razor pipeline is unavailable.
variants.idiom_name: Scriban Template.Parse + Render with a POCO model
pitfalls: Member access follows the renamer convention and undefined members render empty rather than throwing, so a template can silently lose a value; keep one render test per template.
Scriban is a scripting engine as well as a template engine: exposing services to it turns templates into code, so hand it a narrow model.
Rendering templates from untrusted sources requires the sandbox/runtime limits to be configured deliberately; a default ScriptObject model is not a boundary.
